sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: The verb agrees with its subject. One thing: *van* (is). Several things: *vannak* (are). The noun is plural in both cases, so a plural noun and *vannak* go together: *A könyv itt van.* but *A könyvek itt vannak.* To ask where several things are, use *hol vannak*: *Hol vannak a székek?*

English changes 'is' to 'are' as well, so this feels familiar, but be careful with *sok*: after *sok* the noun stays singular and so does the verb, as you saw in unit 6: *Sok könyv van itt*, not *vannak*.
